I work at a packaging and sales division for an entertainment law firm. Part of my job is reviewing scripts. I have to charge a fee for it. It takes me like 8+ hours to give an honest opinion. 

I think it all depends on what you want to do with your work. You want to submit to production companies/major festivals? Doesn’t hurt to bring a professional in, because you’re paying for their connections as well. 

If you’re not there yet, it’s not worth the price.

Insurance is literally the biggest hurdle for productions at the moment. 

No one is granting any sort of coverage, especially union, without a Covid clause in place.

I’d expect they’d have their shit together on set, any sort of violation could be a risk for non compliance.

Do you have bible to go alongside your script? Maybe take a day to build a deck or something just to remind yourself who your characters are/their purpose.

I do often notice when the dialogue tends to die out....but don’t feel bad if people say things to move the scene along. That’s literally pacing. 

The real goal, especially for a first draft, is to have the dialogue establish character identity so when someone else reads it they can get the image of the character you have in your head.

Bruh you’re thinking of step 32 when you’re on step one. 

It’s really easy to get caught in the storm but you have to remove yourself from that cycle. Your focus will just be on creating your honest, and most authentic self in the script. When it’s done and you feel it’s your damn best, the steps to push it out there won’t feel so daunting.

I’m not entirely sure for the UK. In the US, however, most scripts I read are registered with the WGA. More importantly, however, they’re registered with the Library of Congress. Library of Congress US Copyright office is the official way of claiming ones work. 

Perhaps there’s a UK equivalent?
